edbDesc: A force on a particle suspended in the field of a sound wave arising from the scattering of the acoustic waves on the particle.
title: Acoustic radiation pressure
description: A strong sound wave pushes steadily on whatever it hits, and in a standing wave small beads or droplets get trapped and float in mid-air at the quiet spots. Lord Rayleigh worked out the push in 1902; today it levitates samples in labs, sorts cells on chips and lets you feel buttons in mid-air.
effect: a strong sound wave pushes steadily on objects and can float them in mid-air
usedIn: Acoustic levitators for containerless lab chemistry
Acoustic tweezers that sort blood cells on a chip
strength: Weak: ultrasound can float droplets and foam beads a few millimetres across, but the force is only a few thousandths of a newton.
pickWhy: A clear named effect that moves and holds things without touching them, with many uses still untried.
